facts: $\underset{\sim}{i}$ is the vector one unit to the right and $\underset{\sim}{j}$ is the vector one unit up.
The forms $(x,y)$, $x\underset{\sim}{i}+y\underset{\sim}{j}$ and $\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix}$ all describe the same vector.
A positive first component means right and a negative one means left; a positive second component means up and a negative one means down.
The order is always across then up, so $6\underset{\sim}{j}+7\underset{\sim}{i}$ is written $\begin{pmatrix}7\\6\end{pmatrix}$.
A missing term means that component is zero, so $4\underset{\sim}{i}$ is the column $\begin{pmatrix}4\\0\end{pmatrix}$.
In three dimensions a third component uses $\underset{\sim}{k}$, giving $x\underset{\sim}{i}+y\underset{\sim}{j}+z\underset{\sim}{k}=\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{pmatrix}$.
Printed vectors are bold, as in $\mathbf{a}$, and handwritten ones carry a tilde underneath, as in $\underset{\sim}{a}$.
steps: Read the horizontal component: how far right (positive) or left (negative).
Read the vertical component: how far up (positive) or down (negative).
Write the components in that order, in the form the question asks for.

foundation.solution_text:
There is no $\underset{\sim}{j}$ term, so the vertical component is $0$.
$7\underset{\sim}{i}$
$=\begin{pmatrix}7\\0\end{pmatrix}$

The horizontal component is $0$, so there is no $\underset{\sim}{i}$ term.
$\begin{pmatrix}0\\-6\end{pmatrix}$
$=-6\underset{\sim}{j}$

From tail to tip the arrow goes $5$ units right and $2$ units up.
$\underset{\sim}{v}=\begin{pmatrix}5\\2\end{pmatrix}$

From tail to tip the arrow goes $3$ units left and $4$ units down.
$\underset{\sim}{w}=-3\underset{\sim}{i}-4\underset{\sim}{j}$

The $\underset{\sim}{i}$ term goes on top, whichever order it is printed in.
$3\underset{\sim}{j}+8\underset{\sim}{i}$
$=8\underset{\sim}{i}+3\underset{\sim}{j}$
$=\begin{pmatrix}8\\3\end{pmatrix}$

development.solution_text:
From tail to tip the arrow goes $5$ units right and $4$ units down.
$\underset{\sim}{u}=\begin{pmatrix}5\\-4\end{pmatrix}$

The vertical component is $-1$, so its term is $-\underset{\sim}{j}$.
$\begin{pmatrix}-19\\-1\end{pmatrix}$
$=-19\underset{\sim}{i}-\underset{\sim}{j}$

mastery.solution_text:
Put the $\underset{\sim}{i}$ component on top and the $\underset{\sim}{j}$ component below.
$-47\underset{\sim}{j}-\underset{\sim}{i}$
$=-\underset{\sim}{i}-47\underset{\sim}{j}$
$=\begin{pmatrix}-1\\-47\end{pmatrix}$
